source_document.body:
U.S. Army Vice Chief of Staff, Gen. Christopher LaNeve, speaks at the 2026 AUSA Annual Meeting and Exposition in Washington, D.C., Oct. 12, 2026. (U.S. Army photo by Staff Sgt. Alexander Nieves)
WASHINGTON — The White House has officially nominated Gen. Christopher LaNeve to be the Army’s Chief of Staff after several months of serving as both the vice chief and acting chief of the service, according to a recently posted Congressional notification .
President Donald Trump has also nominated Lt. Gen. Marcus Evan s to succeed LaNeve as t he service’s vice chief.
LaNeve has been acting as the Army’s to p uniformed leader since Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ousted former Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George in April . LaNeve, a former 82nd Airborne Division commander, took over after then-Vice Chief Gen. James Mingus retired a full two years earlier than expected . Notably, LaNeve served as a military aide to Hegseth prior to his current role.
Though LaNeve has only served as chief in an acting capacity, he has already made considerable change s to the service. He’s issued ne w doctrine on how the Army prepares for conflict through his “ How the Army Fights ” guidance, created a new Program Acquisition Executive for autonomy, redesignated the service’s Futures and Concepts Command as the new Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command and more.
LaNeve’s nomination also comes as the Republican-led Congress approaches its scheduled end in January, potentially complicating his path to confirmation if the process extends into the new Congress. That gives current lawmakers a strong incentive to confirm the LaNeve before January.
Meanwhile, Evans most recently served as the special assistant to the commanding general for US Army Pacific Command, according to his service bio page . Prior to that, he was commanding general of the 25th Infantry Division and served as chief of staff at US Special Operations Command. He also served in combat in both Afghanistan and Iraq.
The nominations come as the Army remains without permanently confirmed top uniform or civilian leadership. T hen-Secretary Dan Driscoll resigned in September, and Adam Telle is currently serving as acting secretary. The White House has yet to nominate an official successor to fill the role.
